tasks.title: ensureAttemptRecord: decide the attempt record's beforeSha under the lock (close the silent review-skip race)
tasks.description:
Close a race that can silently skip a task's post-task review.

THE BUG: when a task is picked, both callers decide 'does an attempt record already exist?' from a read taken OUTSIDE the run-state lock, and only call captureGitSha when it doesn't:
- src/commands/run.ts ~646-661: `const priorAttempt = deps.runState.read(dataDir).attempts[attemptKey]; const capturedSha = priorAttempt ? null : deps.captureGitSha(projectRoot);` then a locked update creates `newAttemptRecord(capturedSha, iteration)` if the record is missing.
- src/commands/round.ts ~102 and ~138-151: `roundNext` reads `state` at function entry (before task selection and the HEALTH CHECK, a multi-second window) and uses `state.attempts[attemptKey] ? null : captureGitSha(...)`.
If `cairn task set-status` clears the record inside that window, the locked update finds no record and writes one with `beforeSha: null`. Settle then returns `done` with reason `no-before-sha` and the review never runs.

FIX (src/run-state.ts):
- Export a pure `upsertAttemptRecord(state: RunState, taskId: number, iteration: number, headSha: string | null): AttemptRecord` that operates on a state object already inside a caller's `store.update`: if no record exists for the task, create `newAttemptRecord(headSha, iteration)`; otherwise keep the existing `beforeSha` and set `iteration`. Return the record.
- Export `ensureAttemptRecord(dataDir, taskId, iteration, headSha, store)` as a thin wrapper that does one `store.update` calling `upsertAttemptRecord`.
- Callers capture HEAD UNCONDITIONALLY before the call (a cheap `git rev-parse`) — never inside the lock (run-state locking rule: critical sections must be short; never shell out or run health checks while holding the run-state lock).
- runRun uses `ensureAttemptRecord`. roundNext calls `upsertAttemptRecord` inside the `store.update` it already does to bump `s.iteration`, so it stays one locked pass (task 112 will add orphan pruning to that same update). Remove both unlocked existence checks.
- A re-pick must still keep the FIRST attempt's beforeSha (so the review covers every attempt) — existing tests for that must stay green.

TESTS:
- test/run-state.test.ts: upsert creates with the given sha; upsert on an existing record keeps its beforeSha and updates iteration; ensureAttemptRecord round-trips through the file store in a temp dir.
- test/commands/round.test.ts and test/commands/run.test.ts: a store fake whose record is removed between the caller's earlier read and the update (e.g. a store whose read() still shows the record but whose update() state lacks it) ends up with the captured HEAD sha, never null. Existing 're-pick keeps the original sha' tests stay green.

TDD: write the failing test first, run it and watch it fail, then implement until it passes — all within this task.

LIVE-REPO HAZARD: never run `cairn round …`, `cairn hook …`, or `bun src/index.ts round|hook …` against this repository's root — a task in round 15 did, and left stale run state in .cairn/. Exercise these only through the tests, in temp directories created with fs.mkdtempSync.

tasks.notes:
Closed the attempt-record beforeSha race (silent review skip).

- src/run-state.ts: new `upsertAttemptRecord(state, taskId: number, iteration, headSha)` — pure, operates on a state already inside a caller's `store.update`; creates `newAttemptRecord(headSha, iteration)` if missing, otherwise keeps beforeSha/counters and sets iteration. Returns the live record. `ensureAttemptRecord(dataDir, taskId, iteration, headSha, store)` wraps it in one `store.update` and returns a shallow copy of the record.
- src/commands/run.ts (step i): captures HEAD unconditionally (`deps.captureGitSha`) before the lock, then `ensureAttemptRecord(...)`; `beforeSha` for the review comes from the returned record. Unlocked `runState.read` existence check removed.
- src/commands/round.ts (steps 4–5): HEAD captured unconditionally before the lock; the existing `store.update` that bumps `s.iteration` now calls `upsertAttemptRecord(s, task.id, next, headSha)` — still one locked pass (task 112 can add orphan pruning there). The entry-time `state` read is still used only for the pending-review check.
- Behaviour change: captureGitSha now runs on every pick, including re-picks (the round test 'a re-pick keeps the original beforeSha' was updated from expecting 0 sha calls to 1; the beforeSha assertion is unchanged and still holds).
- Tests: test/run-state.test.ts (upsert create/keep/null-head, ensureAttemptRecord file-store round-trip + recreate after clear); round.test.ts and run.test.ts race tests with a store whose read() shows the record but update() state lacks it → record gets captured HEAD, not null.
- bun test: 1162 pass, 0 fail. bun run typecheck exits 0. cairn.json untouched.

tasks.title: Self-sufficient retry verdicts: carry promptFile and model; assert the failure tail
tasks.description:
Make the `retry` verdict from settle carry everything the /cairn-run run agent needs to relaunch a task agent, so a compacted or resumed run agent can retry correctly. Design rule from round 15: every CLI verdict's output (plus its `next` hint) must be enough on its own — the run agent's memory is exactly what compaction loses.

TODAY: `cairn round next`'s `task` verdict includes `promptFile` and `model`, but settle's `retry` verdict (src/settle.ts, the `retry(...)` helper and `retryNext()`) does not. commands/cairn-run.md tells the run agent to relaunch 'with the same model and prompt file', relying on memory.

CHANGES:
1. Add `promptFile: string` and `model: string` to the `retry` variant of the `Verdict` union in src/settle.ts. `promptFile` = the task agent prompt path (`.cairn_task_<id>_prompt.md`); `model` = the task's resolved model. `next` must name both explicitly (e.g. 'Launch a fresh cairn-task-agent with model <model> and prompt Read <promptFile> and follow it, then run: cairn round settle <id>'), for both `continue` (fallback clause) and `fresh`.
2. Avoid an import cycle: settle.ts cannot import from src/commands/run.ts or src/commands/round.ts (both import settle). Move `taskPromptFilePath` from src/commands/round.ts into src/settle.ts next to `reviewPromptFilePath`, and move `resolveTaskModel` from src/commands/run.ts into a neutral module (e.g. a new src/task-model.ts, or src/task-selector.ts). Re-export both from their old locations so existing imports and tests keep working.
3. Add `agents?: AgentInfo[]` (src/types.ts) to `SettleTaskInput`; when absent, resolve the model with an empty agents list. `roundSettleCommand` passes the agents `loadRoundContext()` already loads (src/commands/round.ts ~328 — currently loaded but unused). `cairn run` may pass its agents too; it otherwise ignores the new fields.
4. commands/cairn-run.md: retries (both `continue`'s fallback and `fresh`) use the verdict's `promptFile` and `model`, not remembered values. The task agent id is still remembered for `continue` (SendMessage), with the existing fall-back to a fresh agent when it's lost. Update the content test in test/commands/init.test.ts if it asserts wording you change.
5. Coverage gap from round 15 (#96): nothing asserts the retry verdict's `failure` field. Add assertions that a failed validation's `failureTail` appears as `failure` — in test/settle.test.ts, and in test/commands/round.test.ts (the `roundSettleCommand` retry case around line 519 feeds `failureTail: 'boom'` but its `toMatchObject` omits `failure`).

TESTS: retry verdicts (validation-failed/continue, stalled/fresh, incomplete continue→fresh) include promptFile and model; model resolution honours task.model, a specialist agent's model, and the 'opus' default; `next` names both; failure asserted in both test files.

tasks.title: Prune orphaned executing run-state records (never awaiting-review)
tasks.description:
Stop orphaned attempt records from piling up in `.cairn/.cairn_run_state.json`.

BACKGROUND: an attempt record in phase `executing` whose task is no longer in tasks.json (archived by another path, deleted, or left behind by an interrupted/misdirected run) is never removed. Round 15 left exactly such a record for archived task #99. Settle on such a task returns `already-settled` (src/settle.ts, the idempotency lookup: task not found in tasks.json but present in tasks.completed.json) but leaves the record in place.

CHANGES:
1. src/commands/round.ts `roundNext`: after reading tasks.json, prune every record with `phase === 'executing'` whose task id is not in tasks.json. Do it inside the single `store.update` that already bumps the iteration and upserts the picked task's record (task 110's `upsertAttemptRecord`), so it stays one short locked pass. On the `round-done` path there is no update today: take one short update ONLY when the snapshot actually shows orphans. NEVER prune `awaiting-review` records — their tasks are archived by design, and a pending review must survive (roundNext returns them first).
2. src/settle.ts: when the idempotency lookup returns `already-settled` and a record exists in phase `executing`, clear it. Never clear an `awaiting-review` record there.
3. Locking: the run-state lock may be taken before the tasks.json lock, never inside a mutateTasksFile callback. Don't hold it across the health check.

TESTS:
- test/commands/round.test.ts: an executing record for a task absent from tasks.json is pruned on the task path and on the round-done path; an awaiting-review record for an archived task survives (and is still returned first); a record for a task still in tasks.json is untouched; no write happens on round-done when there are no orphans.
- test/settle.test.ts: already-settled clears a leftover executing record; an awaiting-review record is not cleared by that path.

tasks.title: Reviewer hook: deny git --output (a write primitive hidden in read-only git commands)
tasks.description:
Close a write hole in the /cairn-run reviewer's Bash containment.

BACKGROUND: `cairn hook pre-tool-use` (src/commands/hook.ts) confines the `post-task-reviewer` subagent's Bash to read-only git inspection: every subcommand must start with a GIT_INSPECTION_RULES prefix (git diff, git log, git show, git status, git rev-parse — src/claude-settings.ts:82), and redirection (<, >), backticks and $( are denied (`isInspectionOnly`, ~line 89). But `git diff`, `git log` and `git show` accept `--output=<file>` (or `--output <file>`), which writes their output to ANY file — verified: `git log --output=<file> -1` creates the file. git rejects abbreviations (`--outp`, `--out`, `--ou` all exit 128), so matching the exact token is sufficient.

CHANGES (src/commands/hook.ts):
- Deny a reviewer Bash command when any whitespace-separated token of any subcommand is exactly `--output` or starts with `--output=`, after stripping surrounding single/double quotes from the token.
- Do NOT deny `--output-indicator-new=…` / `--output-indicator-old=…` / `--output-indicator-context=…` (harmless diff options).
- Update the reviewer Bash deny reason to mention that `--output` is not allowed.
- Headless `cairn run` is out of scope: its reviewer's `--allowedTools "Bash(git diff:*)"` prefix rules cannot exclude an argument; that gap is documented by a later docs task. Do not change src/post-task-reviewer.ts.

TESTS (test/commands/hook.test.ts): deny `git diff --output=x`, `git log --output x`, `git show HEAD --output=/tmp/y`, `git diff "--output=x"`, and `git status && git log --output=z`; allow `git diff --output-indicator-new=+ HEAD~1`, plain `git log --oneline -5`, and the existing allow cases.

TDD: write the failing test first, run it and watch it fail, then implement until it passes — all within this task.

tasks.title: Settle fixes: persist a --before-sha override on a repeat awaiting-review call; pin the incomplete guard's validation-status rule
tasks.description:
Two small fixes in src/settle.ts flagged by the round-15 reviews (#97, #94).

1. --before-sha ON A REPEAT CALL (#97). In `settleTask`'s early `record?.phase === 'awaiting-review'` branch, `const beforeSha = input.beforeSha ?? record.beforeSha` is used only to (re)write the review prompt file when it is missing, and is never saved. So a repeat `cairn round settle <id> --before-sha <sha>` leaves the record and prompt file naming the old range. Fix: when `input.beforeSha` is given and differs from `record.beforeSha`, save it to the record (short `store.update`, same as the first gate pass does with `r.beforeSha = beforeSha`) and REWRITE the review prompt file (unless `input.inlineReview`), even if the file already exists. With no override, or the same value, behavior is unchanged (rewrite only if missing).

2. INCOMPLETE GUARD (#94). The incomplete guard counts a task left `in-progress` at settle unless `validation.status === 'failed'`. That exclusion is only safe because `validateTaskTests` (src/test-validator.ts) returns `skipped` for any non-complete task and only produces `error` for complete tasks. Add a comment at the guard explaining this dependency, and a table-driven test in test/settle.test.ts over every `ValidationResult` status (`passed`, `failed`, `skipped`, `error`) combined with a re-read status of `in-progress`, pinning which ones increment `incompletes` today — so a future change to validateTaskTests or the guard fails a test instead of silently changing behavior.

TESTS (test/settle.test.ts): repeat awaiting-review call with a different --before-sha persists it and rewrites the existing prompt file with the new `<sha>..HEAD` range; same/absent override leaves an existing file untouched; the incomplete-guard status table.
